forensic_report.operating_leverage_analysis: ASML exhibits strong operating leverage due to its massive fixed cost base in R&D for next-generation lithography (e.g., High-NA EUV) and specialized manufacturing facilities. Variable costs are tied to complex sub-components like Zeiss optics. Because of its monopolistic pricing power, incremental system sales carry extremely high gross margins, allowing revenue growth to flow disproportionately down to EBIT and FCF.
forensic_report.moat_evidence: ASML holds a 100% market share in EUV lithography, protected by thousands of patents and decades of trade secrets. It has an exclusive, deeply integrated partnership with Carl Zeiss SMT for optics. Switching costs are insurmountable as leading-edge fabs (TSMC, Intel) design their entire manufacturing processes around ASML's EUV technology.
forensic_report.pricing_power_evidence: ASML has consistently increased the Average Selling Price (ASP) of its systems, with High-NA EUV machines priced over $300 million, up from $150 million for standard EUV. Customers accept these price hikes with zero churn because there are no alternative suppliers for leading-edge lithography.
forensic_report.concentration_details: TSMC, Samsung, and Intel collectively account for the vast majority of ASML's system revenue, with TSMC historically exceeding 30% of total sales. A reduction in capex from any of these top customers, or a disruption with its sole-source optics supplier Carl Zeiss SMT, would severely impact revenue.
forensic_report.business_description: ASML designs, manufactures, and services advanced photolithography systems used by the semiconductor industry to manufacture integrated circuits. Its customers are the world's leading chipmakers, including foundries and memory manufacturers. The company generates revenue through the sale of multi-million dollar lithography machines (EUV and DUV) and recurring installed base management services.

revenue_segments.growth_trend: Growing driven by advanced node transitions

forensic_report.competitive_landscape: ASML competes with Nikon and Canon in the mature DUV and i-line lithography markets. However, ASML differentiates itself by holding an absolute monopoly in Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, which is strictly required for manufacturing all leading-edge semiconductor chips.
forensic_report.regulatory_risk: ASML faces severe regulatory and geopolitical risks due to US and Dutch export controls restricting the sale of advanced EUV and DUV lithography equipment to China.
